shortDescription: By Satoshi SugiyamaJapanese government bond yields mostly rose on Tuesday, though the benchmark 10-year yield bucked the trend, as investors grew wary of taking on interest-rate risk at the long end of the curve.

children: Japanese government bond yields mostly rose on Tuesday, though the benchmark 10-year yield bucked the trend, as investors grew wary of taking on interest-rate risk at the long end of the curve.

The 20-year JGB yield (JP20YTN=JBTC) climbed 2 basis points (bps) to a roughly one-month high of 3.780%, while the 30-year yield (JP30YTN=JBTC) added 1 bp to 4.050%, its highest level since October 9. Yields move inversely to bond prices
The benchmark 10-year JGB yield (JP10YTN=JBTC) fell 1 bp to 2.875%. The 5-year yield (JP5YTN=JBTC) rose 0.5 bps to 2.260%
Investors remained cautious ahead of Wednesday's 20-year bond auction after last week's 30-year sale drew weak demand

"With the Bank of Japan seen staying on course for further rate hikes and uncertainty lingering over inflation and the terminal rate, investors are unlikely to aggressively buy longer-dated and superlong JGBs," said Takayuki Miyajima, senior economist at Sony Financial Group, in a note

Keisuke Tsuruta, senior bond strategist at Mitsubishi UFJ Morgan Stanley Securities, said in a note that investors appeared to be growing more cautious about taking on interest-rate risk, leading them to hold back from buying superlong JGBs and to continue adjusting positions.

"There may also be concern that falling equities could trigger rebalancing by pension funds and others, involving equity purchases and bond sales, which would loosen bond supply-demand conditions," Tsuruta said

Japanese equities extended losses on Tuesday, following Wall Street lower as investors assessed the fallout from tighter US curbs on China's access to advanced AI chips and shunned aggressive buying ahead of Nvidia's
US Treasury yields fell overnight as oil prices dropped and investors priced in further Federal Reserve rate hikes in the coming months
